newsitem.title: USA: CME traders say USDA cattle on feed report neutral.
newsitem.headline: CME traders say USDA cattle on feed report neutral.

text.p: CME traders said Friday's U.S. Department of Agriculture cattle on feed report was neutral for live cattle futures.
The report put cattle on feed (in lots of 1,000 head or more) in the leading seven states, as of April 1, at 107 percent of a year ago.
A Reuter survey of analysts produced an average estimate of 107.6 percent with a 106.0 to 108.7 percent range.
March seven state placements in large lots were put by USDA at 102 percent, slightly below the analyst average of 103.3 percent but well within the 100.5-107.0 range.
March seven state marketings in large lots were put by USDA at 101 percent, versus an average analyst estimate of 100.6. Estimates had ranged from 98.0 to 104.5 percent.
USDA noted the cattle total for the leading seven states of 8.9 million head included 3.43 million heifers/heifer calves, up 19 percent from 1996.
The total of steers and steer calves, 5.42 million, was up just one percent from a year earlier.
